content: The Ravenclaw common room is a wide, circular room with arched windows, walls hung with blue and bronze silks and portraits of famous Ravenclaws, a midnight blue carpet covered in stars, and a domed ceiling. The Ravenclaw common room is furnished with blue furniture. Next to the door leading up to the dormitories is a tall white marble statue of Rowena Ravenclaw. The sound of wind whistling around the windows of Ravenclaw tower is relaxing. During the day, Ravenclaw students had a spectacular view of the Great Lake, Forbidden Forest, Quidditch pitch, Herbology greenhouses and the surrounding mountains. The entrance to the Ravenclaw common room is located on the west side of Hogwarts at the top of a spiral staircase that starts on the fifth floor, and has a door with  a bronze knocker in the shape of an eagle. In order to enter the Ravenclaw common room, a person must answer a riddle asked by the eagle knocker; if they answer incorrectly, they have to wait for someone else to get it right.

content: Located within the depths of Hogwarts, the dungeons house the Potions classroom and the Slytherin common room and dormitories. The dungeons are dark, dingy and cold.

Deep in the dungeons, the Slytherin common room is located behind a bare stretch of wall and required a password to enter. The Slytherin common room is a long, low underground room with rough stone walls and ceiling, from which round, greenish lamps hung on chains. A fire crackles under an elaborately carved mantelpiece, with carved chairs nearby.

content: The entrance to the Hufflepuff common room is located "in a nook on the right hand side of the kitchen corridor", concealed behind a stack of barrels. In order to reveal the entrance one has to tap the barrel two from the bottom, middle of the second row, in the rhythm of "Helga Hufflepuff", which makes the lid swing open, exposing a passageway leading to the Hufflepuff common room. If the wrong lid was tapped or the wrong rhythm was used, the intruder is doused in vinegar and barred access. The Hufflepuff common room is round and earthy and low-ceilinged; and its circular windows have a view of rippling grass and dandelions. There is a lot of burnished copper about the place, and many plants, which either hang from the ceiling or sit on the windowsills. Professor Pomona Sprout, Head of Herbology, brings interesting plant specimens (some of which dance and talk) to decorate the room. Overstuffed sofas and chairs are upholstered in yellow and black, and round doors lead to the Hufflepuff dormitories where copper lamps near four-poster beds, all of which are covered in patchwork quilts, and copper bed warmers hang on the walls.

content: The Forbidden Forest was an ominous wooded area, situated on the edges of Hogwarts but out-of-bound to its students. Full of magical creatures and beings, including unicorns, Acromantula, Thestrals and centaurs, the forbidden forest is known as a dangerous place for all - except perhaps Hagrid. Students are not allowed to enter the forest without express permission from one of the Professors.

Located under the Great Hall, close to the Hufflepuff common room, the kitchens are accessed through a large painting of a bowl of fruit. When tickled, a pear would giggle and turn into a large green door handle, allowing entrance to the kitchens. House-elves can be found preparing feasts for the school's staff and students in the kitchens, which are magically sent up from tables to the dishes on the corresponding Great Hall tables above.

The hospital wing at Hogwarts is a large space full of beds with white linen sheets, where students can recover from magical accidents, injuries and illness. Hogwart's hospital wing is run by Madam Pomfrey, a skilled healer who doesn't ask too many questions.

The Hogwarts library contains many thousands of books, manuscripts and documents. Students are able to read and borrow most titles, although access to the Restricted Section is much more tightly regulated. The school librarian, Madam Pince, is well known for being particularly strict about students making noise and mess - and eating in the library is strictly forbidden!

The Hogwarts greenhouses are the location for the school's Herbology lessons and were full of wild and rare magical plants, including Mandrakes. Professor Sprout is the school's Herbology teacher and can often be found tending to the plants and various magical flora and fungi growing there.

content: Hogsmeade is a uniquely magical village nestled in the Scottish Highlands near Hogwarts, serving as a sanctuary for witches, wizards, and other magical beings. Hogsmeade is the only all-magical settlement in Britain and is located near Hogwarts, allowing seventh-year students the privilege to visit its enchanting streets lined with cobblestones and charming, pointy-roofed buildings. Hogsmeade has shops, cafes, pubs, and restaurants that cater to the magical community. Hogsmeade establishments include: Honeydukes, Zonko's Joke Shop, Madam Puddifoot's Tea Shop, Dervish and Banges, Scrivenshaft's Quill Shop.

The potions classroom is large enough to allow at least twenty students to work and its walls are lined with pickled animals in glass jars. In one corner of the room stands a basin into which ice-cold water pouring from a gargoyle's mouth, while in another is a student supply cupboard. There is a blackboard on which the Potions Master can write the class's instructions. The potions classroom is especially cold, particularly in the winter when students are able to see their own breath. Potions class is taught by Professor Severus Snape.

content: The Unforgivable Curses were three of the most powerful and sinister spells known to the wizarding world, as well as the strongest known Dark spells in existence. They were tools of the Dark Arts and were first classified as "Unforgivable" in 1717, with the strictest penalties attached to their use. The three curses consisted of the Killing Curse (Avada Kedavra), the Cruciatus Curse (Crucio), and the Imperius Curse (Imperio). Using any of these three curses on a fellow human being-Muggle or wizard- results in a life sentence in Azkaban without parole.

A Mandrake, aka Mandragora, is a sentient, magical plant with roots that resembling a human baby. Whenever unearthed, the root screams. As the mandrake matures, it's scream becomes more powerful. The scream of a mature Mandrake when it was unearthed is powerful enough to break glass and might kill anyone who hears it, but a young Mandrake's screams would usually only knock a person unconscious for several hours. Mandrakes stop screaming once replanted in the soil.  When Hogwarts students study Mandrakes in Herbology class, Professor Pomona Sprout them wear earmuffs to protect their ears from the Mandrake's cries.

Devil's Snare was a magical plant with the ability to constrict or strangle anything in its surrounding environment or something that happened to touch it. Devil's snare is composed of soft, springy tendrils and vines that possesses the sense of touch, and resembles Flitterbloom. Devil's snare uses its creepers and tendrils to ensnare anyone who touched it, binding their arms and legs and eventually choking them. The harder a person struggles against Devil's Snare, the faster and more tightly it bound them. If the victim remains relaxed and calm, the Snare relaxes its grip on them. Struggling or resistance to Devil's Snare causes the plant to exert a greater force of constriction. Devil's Snare prefers a dark, damp environment. It would stop in the presence of bright light and recoils from the heat of fire, so a well-placed fire or light based spell such as the Bluebell Flames, Fire-Making Spell, Wand-Lighting Charm or Sunlight Charm would effectively drive it away.

"Now, firs' thing yeh gotta know abou' hippogriffs is, they're proud. Easily offended, hippogriffs are. Don't never insult one, 'cause it might be the last thing yeh do. Yeh always wait fer the hippogriff ter make the firs' move. It's polite, see? Yeh walk towards him, and yeh bow, an' yeh wait. If he bows back, yeh're allowed to touch him. If he doesn' bow, then get away from him sharpish, 'cause those talons hurt." - Hagrid

A Hippogriff is a magical beast that had the front legs, wings, and head of a giant eagle and the body, hind legs and tail of a horse. When interacting with them, Hippogriff should be allowed to make the first move, as that was polite. If offended, a Hippogriff might attack. Hippogriffs were tamable, but only by experts in their care such as Rubeus Hagrid. Although proud, Hippogriffs could also be fiercely loyal and protective of those who had earned their trust

The Griffin was a magical beast which originated from Greece. Griffins have the front legs, wings and head of a giant eagle, and the body, hind legs, and tail of a lion. The main diet of the Griffin was raw meat. Griffins were known as fierce creatures; however, despite this, skilled wizards and witches were able to befriend them. Griffins had a natural instinct to protect treasure and as such were often used by wizards for that very purpose, like Sphinxes. The treasure Griffins guarded could be anything from gold to the plants in a garden. If a Griffin doesn't have any treasure to guard, is becomes distraught. This could be taken care of by simply giving the Griffin a new treasure to guard.

Professor Dolores Umbridge is a short squat woman resembling a large pale toad. Professor Umbridge has a broad, flabby face, a wide, slack mouth, and little neck. Professor Umbridge's eyes are bulging and pouchy, and in her mousy brown hair she often wears a black velvet bow. Delores often wears a fuzzy pink cardigan sweater. Professor speaks with a simpering high-pitched voice that's girlish and breathless, and decorated her office with kittens and other cute pink paraphernalia. Umbridge's thick stubby fingers are adorned with several gaudy old rings. Delores has a big chest. Professor Umbridge, the defense against the Dark arts teacher, is strict to the point of being totalitarian.

Quirinus Quirrell was a young man in his mid twenties with pale white skin. Professor Quirrell often wears a purple turban. Professor Quirrell, the defense against the dark arts teacher, appears nervous and timid. Professor Quirrell frequently stutters and is mostly an incompetent teacher.

Professor Lupin wears a shabby set of wizard's robes that had been darned in several places. Professor looked ill and exhausted. Though still in his early thirties, Professor Lupin's light brown hair is flecked with grey. Professor Lupin has a thin mustache. Remus is good-natured and has an excellent sense of humour.

Moody has a growling voice and looks as though his face was roughly carved from wood. Due to injuries from his long career as an Auror, Professor Moody has scars, and a chunk of his nose is missing.  Professor Moody has dark grey, grizzled hair, and a wooden leg that's described as having a clawed foot. Professor Moody's eyes are described as his most shocking feature: one was small and dark while the other was a vivid, electric blue magical eye that moved around independently from his normal eye, giving him the nickname of "Mad-Eye Moody", or simply "Mad-Eye". This magical eye can see through objects, Invisibility Cloaks, and the back of his own head. Professor Moody has a gruff, surly disposition. Having encountered many dangerous experiences throughout his career, Professor Moody is hyper-paranoid and thought of by many as being delusional.

content: Professor Gilderoy Lockhart was a foppish, handsome Ravenclaw wizard with wavy blond hair, bright blue eyes, and particularly straight and shiny teeth. Lockhart wears flamboyant, flashy robes in a wide assortment of colours. Lockhart is an extremely vain narcissist who claims to have accomplished many heroic deeds. Professor Lockhart is a fake who takes credit for other people's achievements. Professor Lockhart won Witch Weekly's Most Charming Smile Award five times in a row. Professor Lockhart teaches Defense Against the Dark Arts. In each Defense Against the Dark Arts class, Lockhart tells made-up story about his exploits. Professor Snape hates Professor Lockhart.

Professor Slughorn is a fat, bald, old man. Slughorn is short with an immense belly, so large that the buttons on his waistcoat usually threaten to burst off. Students say Slughorn's round stomach precedes him when he entered rooms, and when he stood, the top of his head barely reached Albus Dumbledore's chin. Slughorn has a shiny pate, prominent, gooseberry coloured eyes, and an enormous, silver, walrus-like moustache. Horace Slughorn has a bumbling, jovial personality. Slughorn likes to eat crystallised pineapple. Despite being a relatively good-natured person, Slughorn only has eyes for people who he thinks will go far in life, and thus give him helpful connections. Professor Slughorn rudely ignores people he think won't get far in life, like Ronald Weasely. Professor Slughorn teaches potions class at Hogwarts.

The Quibbler, The Wizarding World's Alternative Voice, is a wizarding tabloid magazine published and edited by Xenophilius Lovegood, father of Luna Lovegood. The Quibbler publishes odd articles, including conspiracy theories and discussions of imaginary creatures.

Hogwarts portraits are able to talk and move around from picture to picture. Portraits behave like their subjects. However, the degree to which they can interact with the people looking at them depends not on the skill of the painter, but on the power of the witch or wizard painted.

Neville Longbottom is round-faced, short, chubby, somewhat buck-toothed, and has blond hair.  Neville is clumsy, forgetful, shy, and many consider him ill-suited for Gryffindor house because he seems timid. However, underneath it all Neville has real courage when the stakes are high proving his worthiness of House Gryffindor. Neville, a pure blood wizard, was raised by his grandmother who constantly brow beat him for not living up to his potential.

Susan Bones is a female Hufflepuff student. Susan wears her dirty-blond hair in a long plait down her back. Once Susan splinched herself whilst practicing Apparition, and in doing so she lost one of her legs. However Susan was able to have her leg successfully reattached by the Heads of Houses but the ordeal left her confidence somewhat shaken.

The Thestral was a breed of winged horse with a skeletal body, a face with reptilian features, and wide, leathery wings that resembled a bat's. Thestrals are invisible to those who have not seen death. In other words, Thestrals are only visible to people who have seen someone dying and fully accepted, understood and internalized the concept.

Centaurs are forest-dwellers with the torso of a human but the body of a horse. Centaurs are gifted in Divination magic. The centaurs of the Forbidden Forest regularly made vague allusions to seeing the future. The downside of their gift for Divination was that Centaurs never give a straight answer to anything, always talking in riddles and being very vague. Centaurs believed that fate is as it will be, and that they themselves are nothing more than messengers. Centaurs believe it's not their place to interfere, unless they have foreseen that they should.

The Manticore is a highly dangerous Greek beast with the head of a man, the body of a lion and the tail of a scorpion. As dangerous as the Chimaera, and as rare, the Manticore is reputed to croon softly as it devours its prey. Manticore skin repels almost all known charms and the sting causes instant death.

Millicent, a female Slytherin student, has black-hair, a heavy, jutting jaw, and a large, square build that allows her to physically intimidate smaller people. Ron Weasley once remarked that Millicent was "ugly," and Harry Potter thinks that she looks like a hag he had seen pictured in Holidays with Hags. Millicent is a mean-spirited and aggressive witch who enjoys bullying other Hogwarts students, mainly by using her large figure to intimidate and even in some cases assault them.

Oliver Wood is a Gryffindor student and Keeper and Captain for the Gryffindor Quidditch team. Oliver was known for his determination and skill on the playing field, and his long lectures before practices. Oliver is well built and burly, and had a commanding presence, especially to those in his team. Oliver gets a maniacal look in his eyes when he's enthusing about Quidditch. Wood has intensely driven, competitive personality. Oliver is singularly focused and determined to creating the best Quidditch team in the school. Oliver's ambition and dedication to the sport was such that he forced his players to train relentlessly, including early morning starts and all-weather training. Wood's obsession with winning occasionally became somewhat maniacal.

Parvati is a female Gryffindor student with Long black hair, brown eyes, who often wears colorful hair accessories. Parvati is twin sister to Padma. Parvati, a female of Indian decent, likes to gossip and is friends with Lavender Brown.
Padma is a female Ravenclaw student with Long black hair, brown eyes. Padma, a female of Indian decent, is more studious than her twin sister to Parvati.
Lavender Brown is a petite, female Gryffindor student with Curly blonde hair, and rosy cheeks. Lavender Brown likes to gossip.

Fred & George Weasley are identical twin brothers with red hair, freckled faces and mischievous grins. Fred and George are both Gryffindor students with a love for pranks. Fred and George Weasley both play as Beaters on the Gryffindor Quidditch team.

Ginny Weasley is a female Gryffindor student with long red hair, brown eyes, a freckled face, and a petite but athletic body. Ginny is extroverted, popular,  jocular, and plays Quidditch as a chaser. Ginny is a skilled broom flyer.

Cho Chang is a female Ravenclaw student with black hair, dark eyes, and a graceful posture. Cho plays Quidditch as a Seeker on the Ravenclaw Quidditch team, and sings in the choir. Cho is a female with Asian features.

Vincent Crabbe is a hulking, dull-eyed, Slytherin student with a pudding-bowl haircut. Crabbe hangs out with Draco Malfoy and Gregory Goyle. Crabbe likes to eat. Crabbe plays the position of beater on the Slytherin Quidditch team.
Gregory Goyle is a thick-bodied, low browed Slytherin student with a permanent scowl on his face. Goyle plays the position of beater on the Slytherin Quidditch team.

Alicia Spinnet is a friendly, female Gryffindor student who likes to play Quidditch. Alicia dislikes those with pure-blood supremacist views, such as Draco Malfoy, and believes there's no difference between pure-bloods and muggle-borns. Alicia is a chaser on the Gryffindor Quidditch team.

Katie Bell is friendly, kind, and gentle Gryffindor student. Katie, a female, plays as a chaser on the Gryffindor Quidditch team and has a strong sense of fairness. It's said that Katie Bell wouldn't hurt a fly.

Angelina Johnson, a female Gryffindor student, is a tall, pretty witch with dark skin, brown eyes and long black hair that's often braided. Angelina is a driven young woman who strives to succeed, whether at Quidditch or her schoolwork. Angelina plays as a chaser on the Gryffindor Quidditch team.

Blaise is an arrogant, male Slytherin student. Blaise rarely expresses his often disdainful opinions in a confrontational manner, and preferring to simply scoff or show disbelief. Blaise was a tall, black boy with high cheekbones and long, slanting eyes. Blaise is attractive, and vain about his appearance. Blaise plays the position of Chaser on the Slytherin Quidditch team.

Roger Davies is a male Ravenclaw student with brown hair and brown eyes. Roger is Captain of Team Ravenclaw Quidditch team where he plays the position of chaser. Roger Davies likes to flirt with the ladies.

Theodore is a solitary male Slytherin student who never felt compelled to join "gangs" like Draco Malfoy's. Theodore is a loner who prefers to do things by himself, although he did join in when Malfoy laughed at Hermione Granger's status as a Muggle-born, which suggests he was a pure-blood supremacist like Malfoy and their fathers. Theodore is clever and inventive, Theodore has brown hair and is "weedy" and "stringy", indicating that he was tall, thin, and perhaps weakly built.
